Jahnavi

Content Writer | Updated on - Aug 3, 2026

The BA (Bachelor of Arts) programme provides detailed knowledge and skills in the fields of Humanities, Social Sciences, Languages, Literature, Fine Arts, Psychology, Political Science, History, Economics, Sociology, Geography, and other domains. The BA programme prepares students for careers in both public and private sectors while developing analytical thinking, communication, research, creativity, and problem-solving skills.

As per the NEP 2020, several universities offer a 4-year BA (Honours/Research) programme with additional research opportunities and multidisciplinary learning. Depending on the career goals and flexibility, students may pursue the course in different modes such as full-time, part-time, online, distance, or integrated.

Course Highlight

  • Course Name – Bachelor of Arts (BA)
  • Course Level – Undergraduate
  • Duration – 3 years (6 semesters); 4 years (honours/research at select universities under NEP)
  • Study Modes – Full-time, Part-time, Online, Distance, Integrated (BA+LLB, BA+BEd, BA+MA)
  • Top Colleges – Lady Shri Ram College for Women, Hindu College, Miranda House, New Delhi
  • Admission Process – Merit-Based and Entrance-Based
  • Entrance Exams: CUET UG, IPU CET, SET, TS DOST, WB CAP (Centralised admission portal used by State)
  • Top Specialisations – English, Economics, History, Political Science, Social Science, Geography, Philosophy, Psychology, Public Administration, and Languages.
  • Average Course Fee – INR 4.2K (PSGR Krishnammal College for Women, Coimbatore) to INR 1.25 Lakh (Shri Ram College of Commerce, New Delhi)
  • Top Recruiters – Media Houses, NGOs, Government Departments, Banks, EdTech, Consulting Firms, Corporate Companies

BA Admission Process 2026

Admission Overview Details
Eligibility Criteria
  • Students must have passed Class 12 or equivalent from a recognised board, with 45%-60% (depending on colleges)
  • Students from any streams (Science, Commerce, and Arts) are eligible
Top Entrance Exams
  • CUET UG, IPU CET, SET
  • TS DOST, WB CAP (Centralised admission portal used by State)
Colleges accepting entrance scores
  • CUET UG – Hindu College, New Delhi; Miranda House, New Delhi; Hansraj College, New Delhi
  • IPU CET – Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, New Delhi; Jagan Institute of Management Studies, Rohini, New Delhi; Vivekananda Institute of Professional Studies, New Delhi
Part-time/Online Admission
  • Admission is mostly based on the 12th score, as entrance exams are generally not mandatory for these modes.
  • The requirement of 12th percentage/scores may vary by institutions
Direct Admission
  • Most of the private colleges offer admission based on 12th scores
  • Colleges offering direct admission: Amity University, LPU Jalandhar, and Chandigarh University.

Ques. What is the BA Honours with Research programme?

Ans. It is a 4-year UG programme introduced by NEP 2020. It includes topics such as research methodology, dissertation work, and advanced academic training, making students eligible for direct admission to certain postgraduate research programmes.

Ques. Which is the most common admission route followed for BA programmes?

Ans. BA admissions are mostly based on merit (Class 12 marks), followed by the entrance examinations and counselling rounds. A few institutions also take direct admission based on Class 12 marks, followed by a personal interview.

Ques. Can a BA graduate pursue an MBA?

Ans. Yes, a BA graduate may pursue an MBA for higher studies. Graduates need to qualify for entrance exams such as CAT, XAT, CMAT, MAT, or university-specific tests.

Ques. Is the BA programme recognised internationally?

Ans. Yes, a BA degree awarded by a recognised Indian university is accepted internationally. Also, graduates may need credential evaluation or specific language/subject tests for higher education or employment abroad.

Ques. What is the scope of BA in the private sector?

Ans. For BA graduates, there are many opportunities in the private sector such as content writing, digital marketing, human resources, customer relations, business development, advertising, market research, publishing, and corporate communications.

Ques. Can students pursue professional certificates along with a BA course?

Ans. Yes, many students can pursue professional certificates along with a BA programme. Certifications such as those in digital marketing, foreign languages, data analytics, graphic design, content writing, financial modelling, coding, and project management may open new diverse career opportunities as well as improve employability.

Ques. What is the learning approach followed in a BA programme in India?

Ans. Both traditional and digital teaching methods are used in BA programmes. It combines classroom lectures, tutorials, seminars, project-based learning, internships, field visits, case studies, research activities, digital learning, and continuous assessment to provide a well-rounded educational experience.

Career Scope and Salary in India

BA graduates have many career opportunities, especially in the fields of education, media, journalism, digital marketing, human resources, banking, public relations, research, social work, tourism, public administration, and so on. Freshers can start their corporate journey in roles like Public Administrator, NGO Executive, Social Researcher, Community Development Officer, Journalist, News Producer, and PR Executive. Apart from the corporate roles, one can also opt for Higher studies or specialised studies (MA/LLB/B.Ed) or prepare for the government exams (UPSC, SSC, Banking, Railways, and State PSCs).

Ques. Is BA a theory-based or practical course in India?

Ans. A BA programme in India comprises both theory-based and practical exposure. Specialisations such as English Literature, History, and Philosophy are more theory-based, whereas specialisations such as Psychology, Journalism, Fine Arts, Geography, and Social Work include practical sessions, projects, internships, fieldwork, and laboratory activities.

BA Scholarships in India

Students pursuing a BA programme can opt for both government scholarships (through the National Scholarship Portal or State Scholarship Portals) and institution-specific merit scholarships. Institution-specific scholarships are mostly available through the official websites or the admission portals of the respective institutions.

The PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS), National Scholarship Portal (NSP) Scholarships, Post-Matric Scholarships for SC and ST students, the PM YASASVI Top Class Education Scheme, the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship for Minority Students, State Government Scholarships, the Ishan Uday Scholarship, and Institutional Merit Scholarships are some of the most popular scholarships.

Other Scholarship Types in India

Scholarship Type Applied By Benefits
Merit-based Scholarships Students with outstanding academic performance Tuition fee waiver, annual stipend, or cash award
Need-based Scholarships Students from economically weaker sections (EWS) Tuition fee reimbursement, maintenance allowance, hostel fee assistance
Performance-based Scholarships Students excelling in academics, research, cultural activities, leadership, or extracurricular activities during the BA programme Cash awards, tuition fee concessions, certificates, and annual scholarships
Defence / Sports / PwD Scholarships Children of Defence Personnel, Sportspersons, and Persons with Disabilities (PwD) Tuition fee waiver, monthly stipend, hostel allowance, assistive support, and other financial benefits

Note: Scholarship eligibility, benefits, and application timelines vary across Central/State/UGC and individual universities/colleges.

FAQ’s

Ques. Which are the top central universities offering BA programmes?

Ans. Central Universities such as Delhi University, BHU, Jamia Islamia, and JNU offer admission through the CUET UG entrance exam.

Ques. Which BA colleges in India offer Online BA programmes?

Ans. Many government and private universities offer Online BA programmes with flexible schedules. Institutions such as

  • Delhi University (Online/Distance Learning)
  • IGNOU
  • Amity Online
  • Manipal Online
  • Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University, Ahmedabad

Ques. Does a BA programme include extracurricular activities?

Ans. A BA programme in India includes extracurricular activities such as participation in literary societies, debates, sports, NSS, NCC, student clubs, theatre, music, photography, and volunteer activities.

Ques. How is life at JNU for MA students? Is it only hectic or do students have fun too?

● Top Answer By Akriti Banerjee on 04 Jul 23

Ans. My friend pursued his M.A. from JNU and according to him, he spent the best years of his life at JNU. He went to many well-renowned colleges and universities in the USA, however, JNU is unparalleled. At JNU, you will learn even when you are having fun. Female students feel safe on campus. Male students are respectful towards their female counterparts. There are no whistles or cat-calling incidents on campus. Females can walk fearlessly from one end of the campus to the other, even at midnight.  Life for M.A. students is very hectic at JNU. It is more challenging than one can expect. If you do not maintain a healthy work-life balance, you will end up spending all your time sitting in a corner with your laptop and books. Even your group discussions will end up being solely about studies. If you feel that it will be difficult for you to create a healthy balance between studies and enjoyment, you can join JNU as a Ph.D. student rather than as an M.A. student, you will then get more time to enjoy and experience life at JNU.Read more

Ques. How was your SCMHRD BA interview experience?

● Top Answer By Bharath Harish on 18 May 23

Ans. My interview process started with registration and submission of the SNAP C form, followed by the written ability test (WAT). The technical WAT had questions related to probability, statistics, histogram, coefficient correlation ratio, and pseudo code. The WAT section had two topics, one related to 'business acumen dependent on data analytics,' and the other involving the creation of a story by connecting two given images. After the WAT section, the interview process moved on to group discussion (GD) and group exercise (GE). The GD topic was whether technology would replace teachers in the future, and the GE task involved forming a political party with given Bollywood stars. The personal interview (PI) consisted of questions related to my academic and professional background, technical skills in Java programming and SQL queries, conflict management skills, and problem-solving abilities. The interviewers also presented a hypothetical scenario where I had to suggest arguments to the CEO for hiring a Business Analyst despite the cost-cutting measures. Additionally, I was asked to draw a graph that compares revenue and vs financial success.Read more

Ques. What is the minimum passing marks for BA in IGNOU?

● Top Answer By Shivani Bhat on 21 Nov 22

Ans. The passing marks at IGNOU (Indira Gandhi National Open University) are Theory - 30 out of 100 / 18 out of 50 Assignments - More than 50% If you fail to score 50% in assignments, you will have to resubmit them. If you score above 30 out of 100 or 18 out of 500 in theory, then you will pass without having submitted assignments.
